verdict: Twilio's revenue jumped 20% to $1.6B and GAAP operating profit more than tripled to $149M, as demand for AI-era customer engagement lifted growth and free cash flow alike.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: revenue $1.56B vs $1.30B a year ago; +16% organic

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: vs $248M a year ago; 24% of revenue

kpis.label: Net expansion rate
kpis.note: existing customers spent 14% more than a year ago

segments.name: Customer engagement platform
segments.note: Messaging, voice, email and customer-data tools businesses use to reach customers — Twilio reports a single segment, so this is its one revenue line, up 20% (16% organic).

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the communications and customer-engagement platform.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to businesses and developers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Growth accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 20% to $1,560M — 16% organic, the rest from carrier A2P fees passed through at cost and a small acquisition — and Twilio raised its full-year growth outlook to 20%.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit is now real
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $149M, up 263%, at a 49% gross margin. Non-GAAP operating income was $326M — the $177M gap is mostly $154M of stock-based pay, a real cost GAAP counts and non-GAAP does not.

takeaways.title: Cash flow is the quiet headline
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $370M, 24% of revenue, up from $248M a year ago. Net income of $161M also included a $22M tax benefit and a $25M share of losses from an equity-method investment.

otherDetail: Other expense, net of $10M (rounded): a $25M share of losses from an equity-method investment, partly offset by $16M of other income, net. A $22M income-tax benefit then lifted the $139M pre-tax profit to $161M of net income.
footerNote: Twilio reports a single operating segment, so revenue is shown as one line. Amounts are rounded to the nearest $M from the release's figures in thousands.
